input.reasoning:
Backlog totals 211 story points across 24 tasks. With only a single placeholder role ("Team member", 1 FTE, $75/hr) available, all work must be sequential/serial for that one person. Using an industry-typical conversion of ~6-8 hours per story point for full-stack web work (including design, build, test, review, and integration), I used 7 hours/point as a blended average, adjusted per task complexity/risk (e.g., legacy migration and payment integration carry extra hours for risk/testing; simple config tasks carry fewer).

Total estimated hours: ~1,550 hours for a single generalist "Team member" role, since that is the only role on the rate card. This is clearly far beyond what 1 FTE can deliver in a normal project window (1,550 hours ≈ 39 weeks of full-time work, i.e. ~9 months solo, with zero slack for illness, meetings, or unknowns), so I flag in assumptions that the role is staffed far too thinly for this backlog and that realistically this project needs additional roles (e.g., backend dev, frontend dev, QA, DevOps, PM) to be delivered in a normal timeframe — but per the hard constraint I cannot invent new roles, so all labour is billed under "Team member" at $75/hr.

I built a most-likely (P50) scenario from the raw hour estimate, a conservative/pessimistic (P80) scenario adding ~25% contingency for integration/legacy-migration risk, and an optimistic (P20) scenario assuming aggressive descoping and reuse (see reductions) cutting ~30% of hours.

Non-labour costs are placeholder/estimated: staging/cloud infra, Stripe fees setup, third-party services (email, SMS/2FA, search index, APM/observability tooling), and a data-migration contingency buffer, all clearly flagged as indicative given no actuals exist.

Priority breakdown allocates cost proportionally to story points within each priority band, using the P50 total.

Reductions identify concrete backlog and scope trims: dropping Low-priority admin/reporting/contract-test items, deferring multi-currency and full WCAG AA pass to a later phase, and trimming legacy migration scope by archiving cold data instead of migrating it all.

scenarios.name: Optimistic (aggressive descoping, high reuse, no major risks)
Most likely (P50, current backlog as scoped)
Conservative (P80, contingency for legacy migration & integration risk)

nonLabourLines.description: Staging & production cloud infrastructure (hosting, CI runners, DB) - 6 months
Stripe integration setup, sandbox testing, PCI-related tooling
Third-party services: transactional email (SendGrid/SES), SMS/TOTP libraries, search index (Elasticsearch/Algolia)
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling & one-off ETL/ops support
Accessibility audit tooling/consultant spot-check for WCAG 2.2 AA
Contingency buffer for unplanned integration/legacy-migration issues (10% of labour)

assumptions: The provided rate card is a PLACEHOLDER: a single generic 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE. No real team roles (e.g. backend, frontend, QA, DevOps, PM) or differentiated rates have been set up yet, so all labour costs below are indicative only and will change materially once real roles/rates are assigned.
No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project yet; all effort estimates are derived from story points and task descriptions, not from past delivery data.

Story points were converted to hours at a blended rate of ~7 hours/point for most tasks, adjusted upward for high-risk/high-complexity items (legacy migration, payment integration, RBAC, multi-currency) and downward for simple config/ops tasks (CI setup, decommissioning).

With only 1 FTE available on the single staffed role, the ~1,550 hours of estimated work (~39 weeks / ~9 months of continuous full-time effort) far exceeds sustainable single-person capacity for a project of this backlog size; this role is staffed far too thinly for the scope described, and timeline risk is high unless more people/roles are added.

Non-labour costs (infrastructure, third-party services, migration tooling, observability, accessibility audit) are rough placeholder estimates based on typical SaaS project costs, not vendor quotes, since none were supplied.
Priority breakdown cost is allocated proportionally to story points within the P50 labour total, not measured independently per task.

Assumed a single delivery team works the backlog sequentially in priority order (Urgent > High > Medium > Low), which is reflected in the scenario risk framing but not in the flat hourly costing structure.

reductions.description: Descope the 3 Low-priority, non-customer-facing items with least business value now: PW-19 (usage analytics/reporting), PW-23 (contract tests vs helpdesk API), and PW-24 (decommission legacy portal) — defer to a later phase.
reductions.effect: Removes ~21 points (~154 hours) of work from the current phase, deferring it rather than cutting it permanently.

reductions.description: Defer PW-14 Multi-currency support to a post-launch phase; ship with single-currency (USD) support initially.
reductions.effect: Removes 13 points (~91 hours) of complex FX/settlement work from the current scope.

reductions.description: Reduce PW-8 Legacy data migration scope by archiving cold/inactive historical invoice lines (older than 3 years) instead of migrating them live, migrating only active accounts and recent invoices.
reductions.effect: Cuts migration engineering/testing effort roughly in half for that task (~140 of ~280 hours saved).

reductions.description: Reduce PW-18 Admin back-office (Low priority) to a minimal read-only screen instead of full inspect-and-correct tooling for this phase.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~56 hours of the ~91-hour estimate for this task by limiting scope to read-only views.

reductions.description: Defer PW-15 full WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility pass; ship baseline keyboard/contrast fixes now and complete full audit remediation in a later sprint.
reductions.effect: Reduces immediate effort on PW-15 by roughly half (~28 of ~56 hours) plus removes the accessibility consultant line item.
